answer.generated: Achieving all conceptions of fairness simultaneously is difficult because different fairness criteria often conflict with each other, such as disparate treatment versus disparate impact. For example, algorithms may prioritize accuracy over demographic parity, leading to biased predictions. When implementing fairness constraints, trade-offs must be made—reducing bias in one group may increase it in another. Thus, balancing fairness requires careful design choices and potentially sacrificing predictive performance to adhere to specific ethical standards.
